'''Bangabandhu Memorial Museum''',{{efn|Its official name is '''Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Memorial Museum''' but is commonly referred to as '''Bangabandhu Memorial Museum'''.}} also known as '''Bangabandhu Bhaban''' or '''Dhanmondi 32''', located in [[Dhanmondi Thana|Dhanmondi]], Dhaka, Bangladesh,<ref>{{cite web |title=Bangabandhu Memorial Trust Meets |url=https://www.albd.org/index.php/en/updates/news/1449-bangabandhu-memorial-trust-meets |website=albd.org |access-date=7 August 2017 |language=en-gb |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808001001/https://www.albd.org/index.php/en/updates/news/1449-bangabandhu-memorial-trust-meets |archive-date=8 August 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref> was the personal residence of [[Sheikh Mujibur Rahman]], who was also called Bangabandhu, the founder and president of Bangladesh.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bangabandhu's birthday today |url=http://www.thedailystar.net/frontpage/bangabandhus-birthday-today-1377277 |newspaper=[[The Daily Star (Bangladesh)|The Daily Star]] |access-date=7 August 2017 |language=en |date=17 March 2017 |archive-date=8 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808032538/http://www.thedailystar.net/frontpage/bangabandhus-birthday-today-1377277 |url-status=live}}</ref> Rahman was assassinated with most members of his family in this residence. In 2009, [[RAJUK]] declared the museum a national heritage site.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-74498 |title=100 heritage sites listed: Gazette notification soon to conserve those |first=Tawfique |last=Ali |date=5 February 2009 |access-date=1 September 2022 |newspaper=[[The Daily Star (Bangladesh)|The Daily Star]] |archive-date=1 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220901005511/https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-74498 |url-status=live}}</ref>

==History==
===1956–1961===
In 1956, [[Sheikh Mujibur Rahman]], the industry minister of [[East Pakistan]], applied to the government through his private secretary to be allotted a plot in the Dhanmondi residential project in [[Dhaka]], the administrative capital. A year later, the government allotted him a plot in Dhanmondi for {{PKR|6000}}. Until 12 October 1958,  Sheikh Rahman and his family lived in a government building in Shegunbagicha, Dhaka. In 1958, General [[Ayub Khan (Field Marshal)|Ayub Khan]] suspended the [[Constitution of Pakistan]] and imposed [[martial law]].<ref name="Simon and Schuster, Oborne">{{cite book |last1=Oborne |first1=Peter|author-link=Peter Oborne |title=Wounded Tiger: A History of Cricket in Pakistan |publisher=Simon and Schuster |isbn=9781849832489 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EXXGBwAAQBAJ&q=iskander+mirza+martial+law&pg=PA157 |pages=157–158 |access-date=3 November 2016 |language=en |date=9 April 2015 |archive-date=28 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220528173246/https://books.google.com/books?id=EXXGBwAAQBAJ&q=iskander+mirza+martial+law&pg=PA157 |url-status=live}}</ref>  Sheikh Rahman was arrested and his family were evicted from the property, after which they rented a house in [[Siddheshwari]], Dhaka.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/august-15-special-coverage/his-life-struggle-1269613 |title=Righting The Grievous Wrong: His life, struggle |date=19 November 2019 |access-date=4 September 2022 |newspaper=[[The Daily Star (Bangladesh)|The Daily Star]] |archive-date=4 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220904010603/https://www.thedailystar.net/august-15-special-coverage/his-life-struggle-1269613 |url-status=live}}</ref>

As a result of government threats, the family had to vacate the house in Siddheshwari and move to a rented one in Segunbagicha with help from [[Sufia Kamal]].  Sheikh Rahman was imprisoned until 1960; after his release, he constructed a one-storey house there.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://bangabandhumuseum.org.bd/en/page/8/Building-History |title=বঙ্গবন্ধু ভবনের ইতিহাস |trans-title=Building History |lang=bn |access-date=4 September 2022 |website=Bangabandhumuseum.org.bd |archive-date=7 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200607205314/https://bangabandhumuseum.org.bd/en/page/8/Building-History |url-status=live}}</ref> He began living in the two-room, unfinished house with his family, having secured a loan from [[Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation|House Building Finance Corporation]], from 1 August 1961.  Sheikh Rahman had to pay {{PKR}}1,000 advance to get the plot.<ref name=bt>{{cite web |url=https://www.banglatribune.com/national/637316/%E0%A6%A7%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A8%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A1%E0%A6%BF-%E0%A7%A9%E0%A7%A8-%E0%A6%8F%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%87-%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A7%9C%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%9F%E0%A6%BF-%E0%A6%AF%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%AD%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%AC%E0%A7%87-%E0%A6%B9%E0%A7%9F%E0%A7%87-%E0%A6%89%E0%A6%A0%E0%A6%B2%E0%A7%8B |title=ধানমন্ডি-৩২ এর সেই বাড়িটি যেভাবে হয়ে উঠলো 'বঙ্গবন্ধু জাদুঘর' |trans-title=How that house in Dhanmondi-32 became 'Bangabandhu Museum' |lang=bn |first=Mahbub |last=Hasan |date=15 August 2020 |access-date=14 August 2022 |website=[[Bangla Tribune]] |archive-date=14 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220814203420/https://www.banglatribune.com/national/637316/%E0%A6%A7%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A8%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A1%E0%A6%BF-%E0%A7%A9%E0%A7%A8-%E0%A6%8F%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%87-%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A7%9C%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%9F%E0%A6%BF-%E0%A6%AF%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%AD%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%AC%E0%A7%87-%E0%A6%B9%E0%A7%9F%E0%A7%87-%E0%A6%89%E0%A6%A0%E0%A6%B2%E0%A7%8B |url-status=live}}</ref>

===1961–1975===
Sheikh Rahman's youngest son [[Sheikh Russel]] was born in this house on 18 October 1964.<ref name=unb>{{cite web |url=https://unb.com.bd/category/Lifestyle/bangabandhu-memorial-museum-witness-to-history-and-tragedy/56035 |title=Bangabandhu Memorial Museum: Witness to History and Tragedy |first=Rifat |last=Tabassam |date=15 August 2022 |access-date=31 August 2022 |website=[[United News of Bangladesh]] |archive-date=28 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220828182856/https://unb.com.bd/category/Lifestyle/bangabandhu-memorial-museum-witness-to-history-and-tragedy/56035 |url-status=live}}</ref> In 1966, the house was extended to two storeys and became a complete residential building where many important events in the political history of Pakistan, such as the [[six point movement]], [[1969 East Pakistan mass uprising]], [[1970 Pakistani general election]], occurred. It was the centre of political activities of  Sheikh Rahman and the [[All Pakistan Awami Muslim League|Pakistan Awami League]].<ref name=bt/> On the night of 25 to 26 March 1971,  Sheikh Rahman [[Proclamation of Bangladeshi Independence|proclaimed the independence of Bangladesh]] in the house shortly before the [[Pakistani army]] arrested him.<ref>{{cite web |author=Ahsan |first=Syed Badrul |author-link=Syed Badrul Ahsan |date=15 August 2022 |title=Dhanmondi 32, Bangabandhu and our history |url=https://bdnews24.com/opinion/comment/wvzlvqf9oj |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220826220832/https://bdnews24.com/opinion/comment/wvzlvqf9oj |archive-date=26 August 2022 |access-date=4 September 2022 |website=[[Bdnews24.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ludden |first=David |date=2011 |title=The Politics of Independence in Bangladesh |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23017911 |journal=Economic and Political Weekly |volume=46 |issue=35 |pages=84 |jstor=23017911 |issn=0012-9976 |via=[[JSTOR]] |access-date=20 August 2022 |archive-date=20 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220820193156/https://www.jstor.org/stable/23017911 |url-status=live}}</ref> 

The house was damaged during the 1971 war, after which it was repaired. After  Sheikh Rahman returned from Pakistan, he and his family returned to the house, where they lived from February 1972 to August 1975.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://eisamay.indiatimes.com/eisamaygold/culture/bangabandhu-bhaban-in-dhaka-bangladesh/story/77285516.cms |title=বাড়ির ঠিকানা ৩২ নম্বর ধানমন্ডি |trans-title=House address is 32 Dhanmondi |lang=bn |date=25 August 2020 |access-date=14 August 2022 |newspaper=[[The Times of India]] |archive-date=14 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220814203348/https://eisamay.indiatimes.com/eisamaygold/culture/bangabandhu-bhaban-in-dhaka-bangladesh/story/77285516.cms |url-status=live}}</ref> On 15 August 1975, disgruntled army officers [[assassination of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman|assassinated  Sheikh Rahman]], his wife [[Sheikh Fazilatunnesa Mujib]], and their sons [[Sheikh Kamal]], [[Sheikh Jamal]] and Sheikh Russel.{{efn|At that time [[Sheikh Hasina]] and [[Sheikh Rehana]], Mujib's daughters, were in [[West Germany]].}}<ref>{{cite news |title=AL organises month-long programmes to mark National Mourning Day |url=http://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/politics/2017/08/02/al-organises-month-long-programmes-mark-national-mourning-day/ |newspaper=Dhaka Tribune |access-date=7 August 2017 |archive-date=7 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170807234235/http://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/politics/2017/08/02/al-organises-month-long-programmes-mark-national-mourning-day/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=68th birthday of Sheikh Kamal observed |url=http://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/2017/08/05/68th-birthday-sheikh-kamal-observed/ |newspaper=Dhaka Tribune |access-date=7 August 2017 |archive-date=14 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220814203351/https://archive.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/2017/08/05/68th-birthday-sheikh-kamal-observed |url-status=live}}</ref>

===1975–1994===
The military government acquired the house after it came to power on 15 August 1975. The [[Sheikh–Wazed family]] was forbidden to enter the house so [[Sheikh Hasina]] was not allowed inside after she returned to Bangladesh on 17 May 1981. On 10 June that year, Sheikh Hasina obtained ownership of the house when she paid a loan installment; the house was put up for auction due to non-payment of installments of the loan given for construction of the building.<ref name=bt/> On 12 June 1981, the house was officially handed to the surviving family members of  Sheikh Rahman's family; Hasina later found  Sheikh Rahman's diaries in the building and they were later published in the form of memoirs.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.thedailystar.net/book-reviews/karagarer-rojnamcha-jail-diary-difference-1407826 |title=Karagarer Rojnamcha: A Jail Diary with a Difference |date=20 May 2017 |work=The Daily Star |access-date=4 December 2017 |language=en |archive-date=29 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171129110229/http://www.thedailystar.net/book-reviews/karagarer-rojnamcha-jail-diary-difference-1407826 |url-status=live}}</ref> Sheikh Hasina continued to live in the government quarter in [[Mohakhali]] with her husband after obtaining ownership of her father's house, after which she used it for political purposes.<ref name=bt/>

===Conversion to a museum===

After Sheikh Hasina obtained ownership of the residence, she announced it would be converted into a museum, having had the idea after she was arrested for attending a political program during the [[1990 Mass Uprising in Bangladesh]]. [[Sufia Kamal]], [[Baby Maudud]], [[Gaziul Haque]], [[Pavel Rahman]] and many others helped convert the house into a museum.<ref name=bt/> The museum was inaugurated on 14 August 1994, and it was handed to [[Bangabandhu Memorial Trust]] to turn it into a museum on 6 September 1994.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tracing the beginnings of the Bangabandhu Memorial Trust |url=http://www.dhakatribune.com/magazine/weekend-tribune/2016/08/25/tracing-beginnings-bangabandhu-memorial-trust/ |newspaper=Dhaka Tribune |access-date=7 August 2017 |archive-date=8 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808035615/http://www.dhakatribune.com/magazine/weekend-tribune/2016/08/25/tracing-beginnings-bangabandhu-memorial-trust/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The trust selected architects [[Ehsan Khan (architect)|Ehsan Khan]], Ishtiaque Jahir and Iqbal Habib from an architectural design competition.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.ittefaq.com.bd/610011/চিরায়ত-স্থাপত্যে-চিরন্তন-মুজিব |trans-title=Interview: Architect Ehsan Khan; Eternal Mujib in traditional architecture |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220815135304/https://www.ittefaq.com.bd/610011/%E0%A6%9A%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BE%E0%A7%9F%E0%A6%A4-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A5%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%AA%E0%A6%A4%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AF%E0%A7%87-%E0%A6%9A%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%A8-%E0%A6%AE%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%9C%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AC |title=সাক্ষাৎকার: স্থপতি এহসান খান; চিরায়ত স্থাপত্যে চিরন্তন মুজিব |lang=bn |date=15 August 2022 |access-date=15 August 2022 |archive-date=15 August 2022 |url-status=live |author=Syed Tawsif Monowar |newspaper=[[The Daily Ittefaq|Ittefaq]]}}</ref> During the conversion, the trust preserved the original structure of the house.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bd-pratidin.com/last-page/2015/08/15/100099 |title=ইতিহাসজুড়ে ধানমন্ডি ৩২ |trans-title=Dhanmondi 32 throughout history |lang=bn |date=15 August 2015 |access-date=14 August 2022 |newspaper=[[Bangladesh Pratidin]] |archive-date=14 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220814203349/https://www.bd-pratidin.com/last-page/2015/08/15/100099 |url-status=live}}</ref> On 20 August 2011, the museum was extended by building a new six-storey structure adjacent to the house.<ref name=bt/>

===Memorandum of understanding===
The Bangabandhu Memorial Museum signed a [[memorandum of understanding]] (MOU) with [[National Museum, New Delhi]], on 17 December 2020 following a virtual summit between India and Bangladesh, aimed at facilitating knowledge-sharing between the two museums on training, the conservation of fabrics and the curation of exhibits.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.newagebd.net/article/124546/bangabandhu-memorial-museum-natl-museum-of-india-ink-mou |title=Bangabandhu Memorial Museum, Nat'l Museum of India ink MoU |date=17 December 2020 |access-date=31 August 2022 |website=New Age |archive-date=31 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220831221602/https://www.newagebd.net/article/124546/bangabandhu-memorial-museum-natl-museum-of-india-ink-mou |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Description==
The ground floor of the house has a drawing room, a reading room and a kitchen. The drawing room was used for political discussions and has housed a gallery since the house became a museum.<ref name=des>{{cite news |url=https://www.daily-sun.com/post/395722/Bangabandhu-Memorial-Museum:-A-heritage-tourism-site |title=Bangabandhu Memorial Museum: A heritage tourism site |date=28 May 2019 |access-date=31 August 2022 |newspaper=[[Daily Sun (Bangladesh)|Daily Sun]] |archive-date=28 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220828182858/https://www.daily-sun.com/post/395722/Bangabandhu-Memorial-Museum:-A-heritage-tourism-site |url-status=live}}</ref> On the second floor is Sheikh Hasina's bedroom, and those of Sheikh Rahman, Sheikh Jamal, Sheikh Kamal and [[Sheikh Rehana]]. Adjacent to Sheikh Rahman's bedroom is a room where he used to watch television and eat meals with his family.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.channelionline.com/%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%99%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A7%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AE%E0%A7%83%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AE%E0%A7%9F-%E0%A6%A7%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A8%E0%A6%AE/ |title=বঙ্গবন্ধুর স্মৃতিময় ধানমন্ডি ৩২ নম্বর বাড়ি |trans-title=Bangabandhu's memorial Dhanmondi house number 32 |lang=bn |first=Kazi |last=Imdad |date=13 August 2018 |access-date=14 August 2022 |website=Channelionline.com |publisher=[[Channel i]] |archive-date=14 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220814203351/https://www.channelionline.com/%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%99%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A7%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AE%E0%A7%83%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AE%E0%A7%9F-%E0%A6%A7%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A8%E0%A6%AE/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The museum houses Sheikh Russel's possessions such as balls, aquariums, toys and watches. There is also a souvenir shop,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/shout/news/indian-dhanmondi-32-3095471 |title=Reader Submission: An Indian in Dhanmondi 32 |first=Dixita |last=Reka |date=15 August 2022 |access-date=31 August 2022 |newspaper=[[The Daily Star (Bangladesh)|The Daily Star]] |archive-date=28 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220828182857/https://www.thedailystar.net/shout/news/indian-dhanmondi-32-3095471 |url-status=live}}</ref> which has a virtual section that can guide visitors on a virtual tour of the house. This virtual section also has a showcase that contains several important and historical documents.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://thefinancialexpress.com.bd/public/national/a-museum-that-mourns-bangladeshs-worst-carnage-1597405473 |title=A museum that mourns Bangladesh's worst carnage |date=14 August 2020 |access-date=31 August 2022 |website=Thefinancialexpress.com.bd |archive-date=31 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220831220512/https://thefinancialexpress.com.bd/public/national/a-museum-that-mourns-bangladeshs-worst-carnage-1597405473 |url-status=live}}</ref> 

The new section of the museum houses the Sheikh Lutfar Rahman and Sheikh Sayera Khatun Gallery', which is after the parents of Bangabandhu.<ref name=des/> There is also a library and a research centre.<ref name=unb/>  In a room Sheikh Rahman used as a salon where he often meet visitors and guests, a [[cyclostyle]] was installed after 7 March 1971 which was used by Sheikh Rahman. There is also a personal library, from which he declared the independence of Bangladesh by wireless. A telephone in this room was damaged by the Pakistani army firing on 25 March 1971. At the entrance to the building is a reception hall on the ground floor that was used for official purposes. While other rooms of the museum are open for visitors, Sheikh Hasina's bedroom, store room and waiting room are closed.<ref name=unb/>

News]] |archive-date=31 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220831134139/https://tw.news.yahoo.com/west-bengal-cm-mamata-banerjee-050500868.html |url-status=live}}</ref>
